clue.text: Delhi's turnover backing a drug of Huxley's

indicators.note: backing means moving in the opposite direction, so the words that follow are read from the end to the start

blocks.note: taken as written
soma is the happiness drug of Aldous Huxley's Brave New World; the possessive s comes along with it

explanation.surface: An Indian moneylender's takings are funding a narcotic from a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' reads like business takings in Delhi, but it is a pastry: a filled, folded case of dough. Huxley's drug keeps its possessive 's when the string is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A samosa is a fried triangular pastry case with a savoury filling, an Indian example of a folded turnover.

clue.text: Munro, when climbing mount lower than Godwin Austen?

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means going up the column, so the word is written bottom to top

blocks.note: as in 'as I left' means when
Godwin Austen is another name for K2, so a lower mountain is K1, with the digit 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A Scottish mountain-bagger ticks off a Munro while scaling a peak smaller than K2.
explanation.walkthrough: A Munro is a Scottish mountain over 3,000 feet, so the clue seems to be about hillwalking; here it is the surname of the writer H. H. Munro.
explanation.definitionFit: Saki was the pen name of the Edwardian short-story writer Hector Hugh Munro.

clue.text: Bernstein's heroine has the city in a fever

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so the heroine's name holds the city inside it

blocks.note: Maria is the heroine of Leonard Bernstein's West Side Story
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: The heroine of a Bernstein musical has a whole city swooning.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaria is a tropical disease spread by mosquitoes whose chief symptom is recurring bouts of high temperature.

clue.text: Gardener's gateau?

blocks.note: surface reading: a cake that a gardener might bake or enjoy
setter's reading: gardeners sow seeds, so their cake is one flavoured with them

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the gardener's link to the cake is a pun on what gardeners handle rather than what they eat.
explanation.definitionFit: This traditional British cake is flavoured with caraway, the very things a gardener sows.

clue.text: Thus I often puffed stogie, rolled I see

indicators.note: a cigar that is rolled has been turned over and over, so its letters are turned about into a new order

blocks.note: a stogie is a long cheap cigar
the letter I, then the letter C, which is said the same as see

explanation.surface: A cigar smoker admits to often puffing on a hand-rolled stogie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puffed' looks like smoking, but the definition means 'I' puffed up: the self swollen with pride.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone self-centred inflates their own importance, so the first person is constantly swollen with conceit.

clue.text: Progenitor of M = X, perhaps

blocks.note: surface reading: an equation or code, asking for the source of the letter M
setter's reading: M can be Mother, and her own parent is one generation further back; M is also the Roman thousand, a grand

explanation.surface: A puzzle-setter's algebra asks where the letter M comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: M works twice: as Mother, whose parent the answer is, and as the Roman numeral for a thousand, known as a grand. X stands for any unknown such person.
explanation.definitionFit: Your mother's mother or father is one of the forebears two generations back, an ancestor of M.

clue.text: Berlin brought to book

blocks.note: first meaning: the first name of the philosopher Sir ... Berlin
second meaning: a prophetic book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Someone in the German capital is finally made to answer for their crimes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Berlin' looks like the city and 'brought to book' like being punished; they are a philosopher's surname and a Bible book.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford thinker Isaiah Berlin shares his first name with the Hebrew prophet whose Old Testament scroll bears it.

clue.text: Hot starter containing fish gland

indicators.note: containing means holding something within, so the beginner goes around the heat

blocks.note: a tyro is a beginner, someone starting out
H is the abbreviation for hot on a tap
the ide or id is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A spicy first course with fish in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' wants to be a first course; it is a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: The thyroid is the endocrine organ in the neck that produces hormones controlling metabolism.

clue.text: Tempting appeal from the Queen's Mews!

definitions.text: Tempting appeal from the Queen's Mews!

blocks.clueFragment: Tempting appeal from the Queen's Mews!
blocks.note: surface reading: an alluring invitation sent out from the Royal Mews, where the monarch's horses and carriages are kept
setter's reading: a queen is a female cat and mews are cat cries, so this is a she-cat's yowling come-on to a mate

explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Mews in London houses the monarch's horses and coaches; here a queen is a female cat and her mews are the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the shrill wailing cry of a cat on heat calling for a tom.

clue.text: Out of this deranged Highland tailor?

blocks.note: first meaning: the word that completes the idiom 'out of ...' meaning disordered
second meaning, whimsical: one who makes the pleated skirts worn by Scotsmen

explanation.surface: A Scottish tailor has gone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the tailor is an invented word: one who makes kilts.
explanation.definitionFit: Being 'out of kilter' is an idiom for being out of order or balance, so the word completes that phrase.

clue.text: Agent provocateur thrown out of Italy, headless

indicators.note: the cast word is spread out with the country placed inside it
without a head means the country's name loses its opening letter

blocks.note: to cast is to throw, and cast is also the past form
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spy who stirs up trouble is expelled from Italy and beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agent provocateur' suggests a spy, but read literally it is an agent that provokes: something that sets a reaction going.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without itself changing is a provoking agent, and figuratively anything that sparks change.

clue.text: Such a flat ruler extends to 21?

definitions.text: Such a flat ruler extends to 21?

blocks.clueFragment: Such a flat ruler extends to 21?
blocks.note: surface reading: a measuring stick that reaches up to 21
setter's reading: a sovereign offers a rent-free home to someone in favour at the palace, the answer to 21

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat ruler' looks like a straight-edge; here the flat is a home and the ruler is the monarch, who lets such homes out free to favoured courtiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Housing of this kind is granted rent-free by the Crown, as a gift to a royal favourite or retainer.

clue.text: A word to spell

blocks.note: surface reading: a word in a spelling test
setter's reading: a spell is a magical incantation, and this is the classic word a conjuror says

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' sounds like putting letters in order, but it is a magic charm.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the conjuror's traditional incantation, uttered when casting a magic charm.

clue.text: B-be without money     for a German staple

blocks.note: the stutter's opening letter, taken as written
to lack something is to be without it
bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone stammers about going without cash to pay for basic German food.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer is not just colour: it supplies a lone extra letter before the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark rye loaves are an everyday food in Germany, so this is a basic item of the German diet.

clue.text: A (American) man's home is in Cornwall

definitions.note: the definition is a place: somewhere in Cornwall

blocks.note: bo is American slang for a man or pal, with the possessive s
from the saying that an Englishman's home is his castle

explanation.surface: A twist on the proverb that an Englishman's home is his castle, relocated to Cornwall for an American.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at England's far south-western tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Boscastle is a small harbour village on the north coast of that county, in England's south-west.

clue.text: Woman bearing genetic code material

blocks.note: E for east, a compass bearing
DNA carries the genetic code

explanation.surface: A woman is carrying genes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' sounds like carrying a child; it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna is a female first name, and crosswords use any girl's name for woman.

clue.text: Narcissus without his reflection, say?

blocks.note: surface reading: the vain youth of myth deprived of his image in the pool
setter's reading: a reflected sound, which was also the name of the nymph who loved Narcissus

explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the nymph Echo pined for Narcissus, who loved only his own image; a sound reflection bears her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Without reverberation means no sound bouncing back, and here also without the nymph who adored him.

clue.text: Clan or society for English training

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for society
E is the abbreviation for English
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: A club or society set up to train English people.
explanation.definitionFit: A sept is a branch of a family or tribe, used especially of Irish and Scottish kinship groups.

clue.text: Paddington's origin's a liberal study

blocks.note: Paddington Bear came from darkest Peru; the possessive s comes with it
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: The birthplace of the London station's namesake is a broad-minded place of learning.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington looks like the London station; it is the children's-book bear who came from Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful reading or examination of something, so it is a close study.

clue.text: Brave dog left after second nocturnal predator

indicators.note: after places the earlier pieces behind the short abbreviation that ends the clue

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a brave is a Native American warrior; the Cree are a Native American people
the chow is a Chinese breed of dog
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A courageous dog is abandoned behind someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' reads as an adjective but is the noun for a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: This small American owl with a shrill call hunts by night, catching mice and insects.

clue.text: Naturally sheathed core structure eroded

indicators.note: a structure is something built up, so these letters are assembled into a different form

blocks.note: taken as written
something eaten away has been eroded, as rust ate the metal

explanation.surface: The core of a natural casing has worn away.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a botanical term, so 'Naturally' signals the plant world.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a stem with an ocrea, a tubular sheath of stipules, is described with this word, so it is sheathed by nature.

clue.text: Bent American copperhead

blocks.note: first meaning: an American species of bent grass
second meaning, read literally: a red-haired person, copper-topped

explanation.surface: A crooked American and a venomous snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' looks like crooked and 'copperhead' like the snake; bent is a grass and copperhead a ginger head.
explanation.definitionFit: Redtop is a North American bent grass with reddish panicles, and slangily a person with ginger hair.

clue.text: Lobbyist in for a cut: tread dangerously!

indicators.note: to tread dangerously is to move recklessly, so the words are thrown into a wild new order

blocks.note: every letter of these words is used

explanation.surface: A lobbyist is warned that going after a kickback is risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In for a cut' sounds like seeking a bribe, which suits the lobbyist, but it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with influence among the powerful who argues your case acts as a lobbyist does.

clue.text: Gone from the Labour Party?

blocks.note: first meaning: departed
second meaning: the political wing on that side, the socialist end of politics

explanation.surface: Someone has quit the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is Britain's main centre-left party.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a past participle meaning departed and also names the socialist side of politics.

clue.text: Underground river famous for trout? On the contrary, this is filled with chemicals

indicators.note: the opposite of what was just said, so the two parts go in the other order from how they appear

blocks.note: the Test is a Hampshire river renowned for trout fishing
the Tube is London's Underground railway

explanation.surface: A London tube line and a famous trout river, followed by a twist about chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as written, the clue gives the railway then the river; the contrary order is required. Hampshire is a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass laboratory cylinder closed at one end holds chemicals for experiments.

clue.text: Cave Era fly-trap up-ended

indicators.note: turned upside down so its last end comes first, the whole run is taken from back to front

blocks.note: taken as written
a spider's web traps flies

explanation.surface: A prehistoric cave with its insect trap tipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cave' is Latin for take care, as in cave canem, and English schoolboys shouted it as a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin command cave means be careful, and it survives in English school slang as a cry of warning.

clue.text: Anguilla's captor disturbed a sleeper

indicators.note: a sleeper who is disturbed is shaken about, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: every letter of these words is used

explanation.surface: Someone who captured the Caribbean island woke up a person sleeping.
explanation.walkthrough: Anguilla looks like the Caribbean island; it is the Latin genus name for the eel.
explanation.definitionFit: A pronged fishing spear for catching eels is what catches the genus Anguilla.

clue.text: Look at the list of features in it

indicators.note: in it means placed inside the word that was just named, so it surrounds the list

blocks.note: taken as written
a spec, short for specification, lists features

explanation.surface: An instruction to inspect the specification sheet included with something.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspect is a person's look or appearance, as in a grim aspect.
